result: the three ip#253 findings are fixed. (1) `expect`: the document now says only simulator.run declares it and test.run takes sources, top and runner options; check_params refuses expect on test.run and accepts it on simulator.run (run locally). (2) The SystemVerilog claim about [ZVer] is gone: the page shows only a C++ harness toggling the clock and calling eval. (3) Verdict position: the document says just-before-$finish is a convention (inference) and the gate does not check where the line appears; a run locally with the verdict printed first and output after it passed. Every other source-tagged claim was found in its source and every gate sentence matches the code at the lines cited.
notes: [OTDV]: the smoke test (clock, reset, outputs not unknown, one datapath with simple checks, kept in the sanity set), error tests handled by directed tests because error-checking scoreboards under unconstrained random are costly, and the testplan mapping tests to features are each on the page (the Basic Smoke Test, Security and Error Tests, Testplan and Regression Dashboard sections).

[ZVer]: the page's driver is C++ (a TESTBENCH class whose tick() sets the clock low, evals, raises it, evals, lowers it, evals). It names no SystemVerilog harness, so the corrected sentence 'a C++ harness toggles the clock and calls eval for each edge' is exactly what the page shows. The earlier-clause advice about driving inputs away from the sampled edge is the document's own reasoning, marked inference-level and a fair reading of tick() settling logic before the rising edge.

[VArg]: '--binary: Create a Verilated simulator binary. Alias for --main --exe --build --timing.' matches the document word for word; the --main, --exe, --build and --timing entries agree with it. The page was read in full (this corrects the first version of this record, which stopped at line 1024). Its -Wno-fatal entry ('When warnings are detected, print them, but do not terminate Verilator') supports 'a warning does not stop the build'. No other claim of the document cites this page.
[VSim]: the runtime chapter's Simulation Summary Report (printed at end of run, needs --main or statsPrintSummary) is the 'end-of-run behaviour' the document points to; fair.

The consequence stated, that a warning does not stop the build, holds for both runs. Reported to the document's owner, not edited here.

The document's statement 'the gate does not check where in the output [the verdict] appears' was checked by running Icarus on a testbench that prints the verdict, then 'later output', then $finish at time 20: parse_simulation returned passed with 2 checks. The parser keeps verdicts in a list and tests only their count, their nonce and their numbers (eda_parsers.py:150-154, 191-201).
